text.title: Edge Freshness Report — Output Contract
text.summary: The artefact this methodology produces: an edge-freshness report that records, per probed URL, what the CDN actually served next to what the origin holds, plus the three build-side gates — machine-checkable by the bundled validator.

section.title: Why an artefact at all
section.p: A green pipeline is not evidence. The report exists so the claim "the deploy is live" is backed by a response the edge produced, with its status, its age and its byte count recorded next to the origin's. Anything the build asserts about itself (stamping, allow-list, worker version) is a gate flag; anything about the edge is a probe.

section.title: JSON Schema
section.reference: Filled example of the artefact, safe to copy as a starting shape.
Stdlib validator for the artefact; enforces the forbidden patterns below.

list.item: f1 — a probe with `verdict: FRESH` whose `edge_bytes` differs from `origin_bytes`. That is the exact 735-vs-10 487 shape the methodology exists for; byte disagreement outranks any self-report.
f2 — a probe with `verdict: FRESH`, `edge_status: HIT` and `edge_age_seconds` above `max_age_budget_seconds`. An old HIT is stale until proven otherwise.
f3 — a probe on a path under `/assets/` with `stamped: false`. An unstamped asset URL means r1 was never applied to it.
f4 — `verdict: PASS` while any gate is false or any probe is `STALE`. The report may record a failure; it may not round it up.
f5 — `site` containing a bare IPv4 literal or an `ssh`-style `user@host:port` string. Probe the public name; identifiers do not belong in a committed artefact.
f6 — a probe with `edge_status: UNKNOWN` and `verdict: FRESH`. Unknown is `UNVERIFIED`, never a pass.

example.code: { "artefact_id": "release-2026-08-15-edge-probe", "generated": "2026-08-15", "site": "example.test", "max_age_budget_seconds": 300, "probes": [ {"url": "/assets/js/main.js?v=9f21c0ab41", "edge_status": "MISS", "edge_age_seconds": 0, "edge_bytes": 10487, "origin_bytes": 10487, "stamped": true, "verdict": "FRESH"}, {"url": "/index.html", "edge_status": "DYNAMIC", "edge_age_seconds": 0, "edge_bytes": 24310, "origin_bytes": 24310, "stamped": true, "verdict": "FRESH"} ], "gates": {"asset_stamp_check": true, "deploy_allow_list": true, "sw_registration_versioned": true, "navigations_network_first": true}, "verdict": "PASS" }

example.note: Five violations: f1 (735 vs 10 487 called FRESH), f2 (HIT aged 280 134 s against a 300 s budget), f3 (unstamped asset path), f4 (PASS over two false gates), f5 (an address where the public name belongs). This is the measured 2026-07-28 incident written out as an artefact — every field the pipeline never looked at.

list.item: Every probed asset URL carries a `?v=` stamp.
edge_bytes equals origin_bytes on every FRESH probe.
No FRESH probe is an aged HIT.
All three required gates are true before `verdict: PASS`.
`site` is a public hostname, not an address or a connection string.
